front_matter.title: Null pairs satisfy the canonical anticommutation relations
front_matter.subject: standard-algebra

credit.name: Claude Opus 5.5
credit.source: Co-Authored-By trailer of the commit that added it

sources.locator: Ch. II and III (spinors, pure spinors)

levels.technical: Pairs of null vectors with polar form one half between partners and zero otherwise satisfy, at the level of vectors and with nothing else assumed, the anticommutation relations of fermionic modes. Each hyperbolic plane supplies one such pair, $v = \tfrac12(e_+ + e_-)$ and $w = \tfrac12(e_+ - e_-)$. The number elements $w_i v_i$ are commuting projections. The algebra outside the pairs plays no role.
levels.lay: Inside a Clifford algebra, a direction of space paired with a direction of time produces two zero-length arrows that obey exactly the rules for creating and destroying a fermion. With several such pairs you get several independent fermion modes, without building any Hilbert space first.
levels.one-liner: For a Witt basis ($B(v_i,v_j) = B(w_i,w_j) = 0$, $B(v_i,w_j) = \tfrac12\delta_{ij}$), $\{v_i,v_j\} = \{w_i,w_j\} = 0$ and $\{v_i,w_j\} = \delta_{ij}$ in $\Cl(V,Q)$.

proofs.main: By \claimref{std-algebra.vector-squares}, $xy + yx = 2B(x, y)$ for vectors, which gives the three relations at once. Then $N_i^{2} = w_i v_i w_i v_i = w_i (1 - w_i v_i) v_i = w_i v_i - w_i^{2} v_i^{2} = N_i$ since $w_i^{2} = Q(w_i) = 0$. For $i \ne j$, $N_i$ and $N_j$ commute because each of $v_i, w_i$ anticommutes with each of $v_j, w_j$, and $N_i$, $N_j$ are products of two. $N_i + v_i w_i = w_i v_i + v_i w_i = 1$. For the hyperbolic planes: $Q(e_i \pm e_{k+i}) = 1 - 1 = 0$, $B(v_i, w_i) = \tfrac14(Q(e_i) - Q(e_{k+i})) = \tfrac12$, and vectors from different planes are orthogonal.
